sections.h2: What does a seller face first in Neptune Township?
sections.html:
Neptune's gatekeeper is Code Enforcement. A Certificate of Inspection has to be in hand before a buyer can move in, and the township's checklist backs that rule with fines up to $2,000. The township covers 8.13 square miles of land in Monmouth County, running from the ocean at Ocean Grove to the Garden State Parkway.

This page sets out the township's numbers and neighborhoods, the inspection checklist, rental rules, tax dates and county recording, and ends with how an as-is cash sale compares with a listing.

sections.h2: How does Neptune compare on income, age and home values?
sections.html:
The July 2025 population estimate is 28,273, only 0.4% above the 2020 base. Neptune had 27,935 residents in 2010 and 28,061 in 2020, so the township has been about the same size for years.

sections.h2: Which Neptune neighborhoods draw different buyers?
sections.html:
Neptune became a township on February 26, 1879, cut from Ocean Township. It later gave up land to Neptune City and Bradley Beach, and a short-lived 1920 split of Ocean Grove was reversed in 1921.

Today buyers shop by neighborhood. Ocean Grove is a 220-acre Victorian seaside district on the National Register, bounded by Fletcher Lake, Route 71, Lake Wesley and the Atlantic, and its Camp Meeting Association dates to 1869. Shark River Hills sits along the estuary on the south border. Mid-Town is in a township-led revitalization, and West Neptune holds the Route 66 commercial strip. The Gables, Green Grove, Summerfield, Bradley Park and Seaview Island complete the list.

  • Water is 8.11% of the township's area, including part of the 158-acre Deal Lake.
  • Neighbors: Asbury Park, Avon-by-the-Sea, Belmar, Bradley Beach, Neptune City, Ocean Township, Tinton Falls and Wall Township.
  • Jersey Shore University Medical Center, a 691-bed teaching hospital with a children's hospital, anchors the township's health care sector.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and school information do Neptune buyers weigh?
sections.html:
Five state routes (18, 33, 35, 66 and 71) pass through, and Garden State Parkway access comes at Exits 100 and 102. Bradley Beach station on the North Jersey Coast Line takes riders to Newark Penn, Secaucus Junction, New York Penn and Hoboken. NJ Transit buses 317, 830, 832 and 836 serve the township.

Neptune Township Schools enrolled 3,411 students in 2022-23 across seven schools: Gables, Green Grove, Midtown Community, Shark River Hills and Summerfield for PreK-5, then Neptune Middle School and Neptune High School. It is a former Abbott district, now an SDA district, where the state funds school construction.

sections.h2: What must a Neptune house pass to get its Certificate of Inspection?
sections.html:
Selling, buying or renting without the certificate risks a fine up to $2,000 and as many as 90 days in jail, according to the township checklist. The Transfer of Title application costs $65, is non-refundable, and has the buyer swear not to occupy the home until the certificate is clear, with a fine up to $1,250 otherwise.

Before an inspection is booked, every construction permit and violation must be closed and municipal charges, meaning property taxes and sewer, must be current. An estate needs the surrogate's certificate naming the executor. The application expires after 30 days, and the home must be empty on inspection day.

  • Outside: house numbers at least 3 inches tall, no flaking paint, gutters and downspouts attached, safe railings and walks, and a trash and recycling cart left behind.
  • Inside: smoke detectors on every level, carbon monoxide alarms near bedrooms where required, GFCI outlets in kitchens and baths, and a marked furnace shut-off.
  • Unused oil tanks come out or get filled, which requires a demolition permit.
  • Wood stoves and fireplaces need a certified chimney sweep's letter.

Code Enforcement works from 25 Neptune Boulevard, phone 732-988-5200, extension 260, and the township's forms page takes online applications.

sections.h2: How do Neptune's rental and short-term rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Neptune separates rentals into categories. A standard rental application is for leases of a year (365 days) or longer, and a pre-1978 building needs a lead certificate or lead inspection. Short-term rentals are filed per season: winter runs October 1 to May 22 and summer runs May 23 to September 30.

Tenants complicate a sale because the unit must be vacant when the inspector visits. Match move-out dates to your closing date, and ask Code Enforcement whether the buyer needs an owner-occupancy certificate or a rental certificate once the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: When are Neptune taxes billed, and who handles an assessment error?
sections.html:
Installments are the first of February, May, August and November, each with ten days of grace. Arrears up to $1,500 carry 8% a year and larger balances carry 18%, and a penalty of up to 6% may be added to unpaid balances above $10,000 at year end. Sewer bills come separately, on March 1 and September 1.

In 2026 the township mailed its third-quarter bills on July 29 and moved that quarter's grace deadline from August 10 to August 24. A municipal charge still open on November 11 can be sold at tax sale. The Tax Collector cannot adjust an assessment, so errors go to the assessor, whose Q&A describes the 2014 revaluation that took effect in 2015 and the annual reassessments since.

Seniors and Social Security disability recipients can apply for property tax relief on the PAS-1 form, and veterans' deduction forms are on the Tax Office page. Call 732-988-5200, extension 251, for the exact payoff.

sections.h2: Where does Neptune's deed get recorded, and at what cost?
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Monmouth County Clerk's main office, Market Yard, 33 Mechanic Street, Freehold, where recording runs 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. The clerk's phone is 732-431-7324.

The fee page lists $40 for a deed's first page and $10 for extra pages, and says transfer tax is due when the deed is recorded. It also flags the revised fee for sales over $1 million that took effect on July 10, 2025 under P.L. 2025, c. 69. Confirm current numbers with your closing attorney.

sections.h2: Is a listing or a direct cash purchase better for a Neptune house?
sections.html:
The inspection step makes a conventional sale slower when a house needs work. As-is buyers suit estate properties, houses with tenants and homes with unfinished permits.

  • Listing: broadest exposure, especially for Ocean Grove and Shark River Hills.
  • Owner sale: you keep the commission and do the paperwork.
  • Cash purchase: no repairs asked, a closing date that fits you, and the inspection still due before anyone moves in.

Subtract inspection costs, the tax payoff and closing costs from each offer, then pick the timeline you prefer.

faqs.q: Must a Neptune house have a Certificate of Inspection to be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The township checklist lists fines up to $2,000 and up to 90 days in jail for buying, selling or renting without one, and the Transfer of Title application costs $65.

faqs.q: Can buyers move into a Neptune house before the inspection clears?
faqs.a: No. The Transfer of Title affidavit commits the buyer not to occupy the home until a clear certificate exists, and the form lists a fine up to $1,250 for doing so.

faqs.q: What dates does Neptune use for property tax installments?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, each followed by ten days of grace. Sewer charges fall due on March 1 and September 1.

faqs.q: Which items does Neptune Code Enforcement look at?
faqs.a: Permits and violations, current taxes and sewer, house numbers, detectors, GFCI outlets, the furnace, stairs, gutters and trash carts, among others. The township's Certificate of Inspection checklist has the full list.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Neptune deed?
faqs.a: The Monmouth County Clerk at 33 Mechanic Street in Freehold, open for recording on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
